title: 资产成品包只读预检（R1–R6 修复轮）
commit_note: 5e966624 is the coordinator's own commit of the first 29-file delivery; the coordinator's first validation of it returned changes_requested. This repair round's 15 files are delivered uncommitted: this worktree's git metadata (projects/assetlibrary/.git/worktrees/assetlibrary5) is outside the session's writable workspace, so git add/commit are denied (index.lock: Permission denied) and git writes were not retried. The change set is delivered as .runtime/dsh-delivery/changes.patch (197836 bytes, sha256 fbac87a23b1f66594e936117f8836abfb4cd10047b7d6861bd46321b8a6c28d1), verified to reproduce all 15 files byte-for-byte on top of the base commit with git apply --directory (verify-patch-reproduction.txt). The coordinator fixes the candidate and creates the commit.

tests.note: No test was executed in this sandbox in either round. `dotnet test` cannot start: the VSTest testhost aborts with Win32Exception(5) 'access denied' inside Process.GetProcessHandle before a single test runs, and an earlier round additionally hit the 90s testhost named-pipe timeout. `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` fails the same way at NamedPipeClientStream.TryConnect. Nothing here is a passing test. Real evidence produced in this sandbox: Release build of both projects with 0 warnings and 0 errors under TreatWarningsAsErrors plus the full analyzer set; a 19/19 static self-check of the frozen negative and positive examples against an independent Python reading of the same frozen rules (.runtime/dsh-delivery/logs/static-selfcheck.txt); and byte-exact patch reproduction of all 15 delivered files (.runtime/dsh-delivery/logs/verify-patch-reproduction.txt).

risks: Behavioural verification is incomplete: R1-R6 correctness rests on compile success, code review and an independent static self-check, not on an executed test run. The coordinator must run the standard restore/build/test/format gates on the fixed candidate.

Static reparse-point refusal plus before/after stamps plus a final set re-check narrows but does not close hostile concurrent directory replacement (TOCTOU); real NAS semantics and power-loss durability remain unverified (production_path_races).

The frozen fixtures are the only layout evidence: the multipart 'Season 01' directory name and the S01E{>=2 digits} episode width are pinned by the fixtures, so a future 'Season 02' contract change must extend MediaPackageLayoutPolicy explicitly.

MediaPackageShapePolicy.cs (548 lines) and IsolatedMediaPackageInspector.cs (543 lines) exceed the 400-line soft guideline; both are single-responsibility units authorised by the coordinator, with no multi-statement lines or blanket suppressions used to hide concentration.
contracts/media-package/candidate-v1 remains a task fixture only (task_fixture_only), not a production publication contract.

reused_existing_logic: CanonicalLibraryRoot and RootPathComparison (LibraryStorage.Contracts) for the canonical trusted root and its comparison semantics, instead of a second root representation

MediaPackageIssueSink, MediaPackagePreflightCodes, MediaPackageUnverifiedFacts and MediaPackageInspectionLimits reused unchanged, so the frozen 22-code vocabulary, the 7 unverified facts and every budget ceiling stay single-owner
MediaPackagePathBoundary, MediaPackageFileHasher and MediaPackagePolicy reused by the inspector instead of duplicating root anchoring, hashing or verdict assembly
The test suite reuses the existing MediaPackageSandbox composition and fixture records rather than a parallel harness
cross_module_access: LibraryStorage.Contracts (LibraryId, CanonicalLibraryRoot, RootPathComparison, StorageAvailability) and TransferSync.Contracts (Sha256Digest, PayloadFacts) are consumed as published read-only contracts only; no other module's Infrastructure or internal entity is referenced.
contract_changes: No root contract was modified. contracts/media-package/candidate-v1 was never written; the tests now read the byte-exact copies committed under tests/dotnet/AssetLibrary.TransferOperation.Tests/Fixtures/MediaPackage/, whose LF-normalized SHA-256 values still match the fixture manifest's five pinned digests.

The only contract-surface addition is MediaPackageManifestReadResult.IssuesTruncated and the MediaPackageBudgetExceededException port type, both inside this module's own Application/Contracts boundary.
architecture_tests: Release build of services/core-server/AssetLibrary.CoreServer.csproj: 0 warnings, 0 errors with TreatWarningsAsErrors, EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, EnableNETAnalyzers and the CA1501/CA1502/CA1505/CA1506 budgets enabled.
Release build of tests/dotnet/AssetLibrary.TransferOperation.Tests: 0 warnings, 0 errors, including the MSTEST0037, CA1861, CA1859 and CA1001 rules that previously failed.

Domain keeps no System.IO dependency: MediaPackageShapePolicy and MediaPackageLayoutPolicy are pure (no IO, no clock, no environment), so the architecture gate's forbidden 'system.io' token check stays satisfied; path spellings are validated lexically and only then normalized by Infrastructure.

The architecture, database and repository Python gates could not be run in this sandbox (temp-directory and named-pipe denials); the coordinator's earlier run of verify_repository and the v0.1-start gate passed and must be repeated on the fixed candidate.
technical_debt: MediaPackagePolicy.cs was split as the reviewer required: shape/type/identity reading moved to Domain/MediaPackageShapePolicy.cs and layout/media_extension/selected_parts templates to Domain/MediaPackageLayoutPolicy.cs, leaving MediaPackagePolicy.cs as pure orchestration (budgets, real-list comparison, target-name entry).
MediaPackagePathBoundary.cs was rewritten around one canonical comparison form and a native access form; the volume-root containment and Linux same-separator cases are now covered by tests.
MaximumEnumeratedEntries (4096) remains a constant rather than a configurable limit, so an oversized staging directory fails with budget_exceeded instead of a tuned path.
Several CA1506 suppressions carry written justifications; they can be reclaimed once a composition root exists.
